match.reason: No point in the bank covers transformation processes and the four Vs; the systems approach mentions inputs becoming outputs, but it is a management theory, not the operations idea of how processes differ by volume, variety, variation and visibility.

draft.title: Transformation processes
card: A transformation process is the set of steps that turns inputs into outputs. Every operations process has one, whether it makes goods or provides services.

Processes differ in volume (how much is made) and variety (how many different products). High volume with low variety suits a standard, repeated process. Low volume with high variety suits a flexible one.
They also differ in variation in demand, which is how much demand rises and falls over time. A business with big swings in demand needs a process that can scale up and down.
Visibility is how much of the process the customer sees or takes part in. A hairdresser works in front of the customer. A factory that makes shampoo is mostly out of the customer's sight.
draft.remember: A transformation process turns inputs into outputs, and it is shaped by volume, variety, variation in demand and visibility.

a.q: Which feature of a transformation process does visibility describe?
opts: How much of the process the customer sees or joins in
How many different products the process can make
How much demand rises and falls across the year
How many units the process makes in a set period
a.why: Visibility is about how much of the process the customer can see or take part in. The option about different products describes variety, which is a separate feature, so it is tempting but wrong.
a.clue: Think about whether the customer is watching.

b.q: Priya runs a beach kiosk in Byron Bay. Sales are huge in summer holidays and tiny in winter. Which feature of her process is the main challenge?
b.why: Sales that swing between summer and winter are variation in demand, so her process must scale up and down. Volume is tempting because summer output is large, but volume is about how much is made, not how much it changes over time.
b.clue: Look at how sales change from season to season.

a.best: How much of the process the customer sees or joins in

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about whether the customer is watching' points straight to the only option that mentions the customer, so a student can pick it without knowing what visibility means.

proposal.remember: Volume, variety, variation in demand and visibility shape how a business turns its inputs into outputs.

a.q: Which of these operations has the highest visibility?
opts: A dentist filling a patient's tooth
A mill grinding wheat into flour
a.why: The patient is in the chair and takes part while the dentist works, so the customer sees the whole process. The warehouse may seem close to the customer because it fills their order, but the customer never sees the packing, so its visibility is low.
a.clue: Visibility is about what the customer sees, not who the work is for.
